description: Grants the real CI-Server web app (served remotely at http://127.0.0.1:8642 / http://localhost:8642 after the bootstrap page's window.location.replace()) exactly the two app-level commands native 'Sign in with Companion account' needs: open_external_url_command (launch the OIDC URL in the system browser) and take_pending_deep_link_command (drain a companion://oidc/callback deep link that arrived before the page's listener was up). Tauri DOES gate app-level commands per-command — but only once an app manifest exists, which is what src-tauri/permissions/*.toml provides; with no manifest the remote origin could reach nothing, since the gate rejects any command whose invoke.acl is None. A plugin permission cannot stand in for this: `opener:allow-open-url` registers plugin:opener|open_url, which nothing invokes — the frontend calls the app command, whose inner app.opener().open_url() is the Rust OpenerExt API and never consults the ACL. That grant is also deliberately NOT taken: opener's scope is app-wide, so it would hand this origin an unwrapped open primitive (mailto:, tel:) and bypass open_external_url_command's http(s)-only guard. This origin now reaches these two commands and nothing else.
